caption:
Every chip in an Indian car, phone or inverter used to come from Taiwan, China, or Vietnam. In July, a Gujarat plant shipped its first batch out - to a customer in Japan.

CG Semi's Sanand OSAT facility began commercial production on July 4, 2026, shipping its first qualified chips to Renesas Electronics India. Peak capacity: 300 million units a year, built on a ₹7,600 crore investment across two planned facilities. CG Semi is a joint venture between CG Power (Murugappa Group), Renesas Electronics (Japan), and Stars Microelectronics (Thailand). Before 2024, India assembled essentially zero commercial semiconductors domestically - it now has five units in production.

A country that only ever imported chips just sent its own out the door. The first shipment of a lot more to come.

Sources: BusinessWire, Verdict/GlobalData (2026)
